outcomes.text: Study education with methods in context, using the core themes of socialisation, culture and identity and of social differentiation, power and stratification.
Explain the role and functions of education and its links to the economy and class structure.
Explain differences in achievement by social class, gender and ethnicity.
Explain teacher/pupil relationships, pupil identities and subcultures, the hidden curriculum, and how teaching and learning are organised.
Explain how selection, marketisation, privatisation and equality policies shape access to education, and the impact of globalisation on policy.
Apply sociological research methods to the study of education.

units.title: 3.2 Research Methods and Topics in Sociology

outcomes.text: Study research methods and topics in sociology in relation to the core themes, drawing on small-scale research examples.
Compare quantitative and qualitative methods and explain research design.
Explain data sources: questionnaires, interviews, participant and non-participant observation, experiments, documents, official statistics.
Distinguish primary from secondary and quantitative from qualitative data.
Explain how positivism and interpretivism relate to methods, and the nature of 'social facts'.
Explain theoretical, practical and ethical considerations in choosing topic and method and conducting research.
Study chosen topics in sociology with evidence and sociological explanations.

subtopics.title: Culture and Identity: Culture and socialisation

outcomes.text: Distinguish conceptions of culture: subculture, mass, folk, high, low, popular and global culture.
Explain the socialisation process and the agencies of socialisation.
Explain self, identity and difference as socially caused and constructed.
Relate identity to age, disability, ethnicity, gender, nationality, sexuality and class.
Relate identity to production, consumption and globalisation.

subtopics.title: Families and Households: Family, marriage and households

outcomes.text: Explain the family's relationship to social structure and change, the economy and state policy.
Explain changing patterns of marriage, cohabitation, separation, divorce, childbearing and the life course, and household diversity.

subtopics.title: Families and Households: Roles, childhood and demography

outcomes.text: Explain gender roles, domestic labour and power in the family.
Explain the nature of childhood and changes in children's status.
Describe UK demographic trends since 1900: birth and death rates, family size, life expectancy, ageing, migration and globalisation.
Explain the social construction of health, illness, disability and the body, and models of health and illness.
Explain unequal health chances by class, gender, ethnicity and region.
Explain inequalities in health care provision and access.
Explain the nature and social distribution of mental illness.
Explain the role of medicine, health professions and the globalised health industry.

outcomes.text: Explain the nature, existence and persistence of poverty.
Explain the distribution of poverty, wealth and income between social groups.
Explain state, private, voluntary and informal welfare responses to poverty.

outcomes.text: Explain the new media and their significance for the media's role today.
Explain the relationship between ownership and control of the media.
Explain the media, globalisation and popular culture.

subtopics.title: The Media: News, representation and audiences

outcomes.text: Explain the selection and presentation of news content.
Explain media representations of age, class, ethnicity, gender, sexuality and disability.
Explain the relationship between media content, presentation and audiences.

subtopics.title: Stratification and Differentiation: Stratification and inequality

outcomes.text: Explain stratification and differentiation by class, gender, ethnicity and age.
Explain dimensions of inequality: class, status, power, and life-chance differences by class, gender, ethnicity, age and disability.

subtopics.title: Stratification and Differentiation: Class measurement and mobility

outcomes.text: Explain problems of defining and measuring social class, including occupation and gender.
Explain changes in inequality, including globalisation and a transnational capitalist class.
Explain the nature, extent and significance of social mobility.
